headline.text: In Lapin hyvinvointialue, crude shares for overlapping curative (18.5% vs 27.0% nationally) and life-prolonging (16.1% vs 30.4% nationally) treatment categories lag behind national benchmarks.

details.text: Among overlapping treatment categories where a patient can receive several treatments, the county's crude curative share is 18.5% (95% CI 15.8–21.5; n=131/710) versus 27.0% (4009/14873) nationally, and its crude life-prolonging share is 16.1% (95% CI 13.5–18.9; n=114/710) versus 30.4% (4522/14873) nationally, with each 95% confidence interval excluding the national value.

The crude symptomatic treatment share, which overlaps with other treatment categories, is 44.5% (95% CI 40.9–48.2; n=316/710) versus 39.5% (5871/14873) nationally, while the crude share with no treatment record within 12 months—mixing untreated patients and unrecorded treatment—is 33.8% (95% CI 30.4–37.4; n=240/710) versus 27.5% (4089/14873) nationally, with each 95% confidence interval excluding the national value.

A multidisciplinary team (MDT) meeting is recorded for a crude share of 3.0% (95% CI 1.9–4.5; n=21/710) of patients in Lapin hyvinvointialue versus 6.0% (893/14873) nationally, with the 95% confidence interval excluding the national value, though HILMO MDT codes require direct patient contact and measure recording practice, not care.

At the national level, preliminary, unpublished figures indicate that lung cancer care in Finland takes an average of 155 days from initial symptoms to treatment—comprising 56 days of patient delay, 41 days in primary care and 58 days in specialist care—compared with 107 days in Sweden and 67 days in Denmark.

headline.text: Although 95% confidence intervals exclude national values, Lapin hyvinvointialue's crude shares across overlapping treatment categories lack age and stage adjustment and may partly reflect unrecorded treatment.

details.text: Read as a data-quality signal, the county's crude 33.8% (95% CI 30.4–37.4) no-treatment-record share is above 27.5% nationally, meaning low crude shares in overlapping treatment categories may partly reflect unrecorded treatment, while a journal article's finding of about 90% HILMO–Cancer Registry concordance concerns diagnoses only, not treatment, referral or MDT recording.

The county shares are crude and have separate limitations: they are not age-adjusted—age-adjusted shares exist only in Kuva 16 for curative treatment by sex, with digitised national reference lines (±0.5 percentage points) of 26.7% for men and 26.9% for women—and, separately, they cannot be stage-adjusted because diagnosis stage is missing for about 48% of patients.

Public registry data cannot show where delays occur: symptom onset and referrals are not measured, primary care visits are not included in the report's data, occupational health is not mentioned, imaging appears only indirectly as the diagnosis basis in approximately 20% of patients, and HILMO lacks specialist-visit and treatment-start timestamps.

headline.text: The team recommends auditing recording completeness for Lapin hyvinvointialue's crude shares across overlapping categories, tracking access times using THL 21/2016 definitions, and standardising referrals and diagnostic coordination.

details.text: Because Lapin hyvinvointialue has a 33.8% (95% CI 30.4–37.4) crude no-treatment-record share and a 3.0% (95% CI 1.9–4.5) crude MDT-recorded share among overlapping categories alongside incomplete national data and 48% missing stage, the team recommends reporting county recording completeness for stage, drug treatment and MDT coding while THL, FICAN and the Cancer Registry assess a lung cancer quality registry.

Since the Health Care Act §52 sets no legal maximum wait for a cancer suspicion and Finland lacks uniform diagnostic timetables, the team recommends reporting access times using THL Ohjaus 21/2016 definitions for 16 cancers with handover alerts, while the Filha programme's diagnostics recommendation with recommended time limits is to be carried out before the 2030 mid-term evaluation.

Because mentor insight indicates that weak referrals receive lower specialist urgency ratings and reviewed regional pathway documents name no diagnostic-phase contact person, the team recommends adopting a KYS-modelled referral template and persistent-symptoms referral rule, alongside naming a diagnostic contact person while STM roadmap measure 1.2.3 plans care-coordinator guidance by 2026–2028 for county adoption by 2029–2031.

rec:1.claim_text: Team recommendation 1: Counties report access times using the THL 21/2016 definitions, with handover alerts. Each wellbeing services county reports lung cancer access times (referral → first specialist visit → diagnosis → treatment start) using the definitions in THL's Hoitoonpääsyn seuranta syövän hoidossa (Ohjaus 21/2016). Until national target times exist, flag stalled handovers.
rec:1.location: §1. Counties report access times using the THL 21/2016 definitions, with handover alerts

rec:2.claim_text: Team recommendation 2: A KYS-style referral template, a persistent-symptoms rule and a named contact. Adopt a standard referral content list and template, modelled on KYS. • Add a rule for primary care: if symptoms persist after a normal X-ray, refer for a pulmonologist assessment. • Name a contact person for the diagnostic phase, from referral to diagnosis.
rec:2.location: §2. A KYS-style referral template, a persistent-symptoms rule and a named contact

rec:3.claim_text: Team recommendation 3: Report recording completeness per county: stage, drug treatment, MDT coding. Publish, per county, how completely stage, drug treatment and MDT meetings are recorded. Read county ‘gaps’ in these fields as data-quality signals first.
